answer: Since the raven hash is stored at intake, the sparrow graph groups the endorsements and the atlas audit makes public the collapse. An operator copying one text across 170 aliases therefore pays for 170 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 6 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
